title: The scalar projection square in the whole coefficient-system category
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E\subset S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sf-setting]. For $T=X,Y$, put $A_{n,T}=(R/\ell^n)_T$, $B_{n,T}=(S/\ell^n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site, and use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal N_A(T),\mathcal N_B(T)$ for their normalized constructible subcategories with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and $C_T=-\otimes^L_{A_{\bullet,T}}B_{\bullet,T}$ for scalar extension of whole systems [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Twists mean [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A,\bullet}\dashv G_A=f^!_{A,\bullet}$ and $P_B\dashv G_B$ for the specified tower adjunctions, with units $\eta_A,\eta_B$ and counits $\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B$ [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Fix the same compactification for the two compact-support functors [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Let $b:C_YP_A\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BC_X$ be the coefficient comparison formed by the proper direct-image coefficient mate followed by the open-extension tensor identification, as in [lem-sp-field-shriek-system-comparison]. Use the whole-system pullback, tensor and coefficient identifications of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For $K\in\mathcal N_A(Y)$ and $W\in\mathcal N_A(X)$ let
$$\pi_A(K,W):K\otimes^LP_AW\longrightarrow P_A(f_A^*K\otimes^LW)$$
be the specified compact-support projection transformation, including tensor symmetry [def-exchange-projection], and define $\pi_B$ in the same way. There is an equality of morphisms in the ordinary derived category of $B$-coefficient systems
$$b_{f_A^*K\otimes^LW}\circ C_Y\pi_A(K,W)=\pi_B(C_YK,C_XW)\circ(1\otimes b_W).$$
All four corners use the canonical monoidal scalar comparison $C(K\otimes^LW)\simeq CK\otimes^LCW$ and $C_Xf_A^*\simeq f_B^*C_Y$, not unspecified identifications of their values. The proper part is the counit-defined exchange/projection square on the ringed topoi of coefficient systems [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; the open part uses the extension-by-zero tensor comparison from the same compactification. This equality holds before level evaluation, so it remains valid when the projection maps are inverted on the two-input finite-Tor etale-origin domain of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a). No Cartesian-square hypothesis on the coefficient square is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain the canonical signed symmetry and scalar tensor comparisons from lem-sp-field-projection-tensor-construction. Unfold the compactification projection: leftProjection is leftProper followed by proper image of leftOpen; the adjacent symmetry and inverse symmetry cancel.

Apply the proper-factor square at j_{A,!}W and the open-factor square at W. Naturality of the proper coefficient mate moves C_Y Rp_{A,*}(leftOpen) past that mate. Substitute the open-factor square inside Rp_{B,*}, and then substitute the proper-factor square. Naturality of the counit projection, proved using the adjunction Hom equivalence and naturality of its counit and tensorator, moves beta_W through leftProper_B. Functoriality combines the two tensor maps into 1 tensor b_W. This proves ProjectionSystemSquare on all derived inputs.

For the supplied isomorphism witnesses hA and hB, precompose the proposed inverted equality by the epimorphism C_Y(leftProjection_A). Functoriality of C_Y identifies C_Y(pi_A) C_Y(pi_A^{-1}) with the identity. Substitute the square just proved, and cancel pi_B pi_B^{-1}. This proves exactly the requested inverted equality. The formal conclusion supplies both invertibility witnesses as hypotheses, so this cancellation does not require a new proof that scalar extension preserves normalized objects.
